:::{#exr-epe-three-sources}
#### Expected squared error from three sources

A prediction $\predval$ at a covariate value $\predvar$ has
squared bias $[\bias{\predval}]^2 = 1$
and variance $\Var{\predval} = 2$.
The new outcome is $\newoutvar = \truemeanf{\predvar} + \noise$,
where $\noise$ has mean $0$ and variance $\varpar = 3$
and is independent of $\predval$.

1. What is the expected squared prediction error $\E{(\newoutvar - \predval)^2}$?
2. If we could remove all bias and all variance of $\predval$,
   what would the expected squared prediction error be?
3. Which of the three quantities
   (squared bias, variance of $\predval$, $\varpar$)
   can a better prediction method reduce,
   and which cannot?

:::
